claims.text: The WTaTiVZr alloy is equimolar, corresponding to approximately 20 at.% each of W, Ta, Ti, V, and Zr.
Intrinsic lattice distortion is the cause of the HEA's enhanced plastic strain and toughness relative to pure tungsten.
Lattice distortion stabilizes a nanostructured or refined microstructure with finer grains and increased sub-grain formation.
The distortion-enhanced microstructure increases dislocation mobility.
Increased dislocation mobility promotes dynamic recovery and recrystallization at service temperatures.
Dynamic recovery and recrystallization delay crack initiation and propagation relative to pure tungsten.
Arc melting and homogenization can produce a fine-grained, single-phase WTaTiVZr microstructure.
The multicomponent alloy's severe lattice distortion generates local stress fields.
These local stress fields stabilize a refined microstructure containing abundant sub-grain boundaries.
The refined microstructure and local stress fields enhance dislocation cross-slip and dynamic recrystallization during high-temperature deformation.
Lattice-distortion strain fields facilitate easier dislocation motion, cross-slip, and dynamic recovery under high-temperature loading.
The proposed dislocation processes improve strain hardening and toughness.
Pure tungsten has more limited dislocation activity and is more prone to brittle failure than the HEA under the stated conditions.
At 1000–1200°C, the HEA will exhibit greater strain to failure than pure tungsten tested under matched conditions.
At 1000–1200°C, the HEA will exhibit greater fracture toughness and delayed crack propagation relative to pure tungsten.
Post-deformation characterization will show a higher dislocation density and more dynamic recrystallization or sub-grain formation in the HEA than in pure tungsten.
The proposed mechanism applies principally in the approximately 1000–1200°C temperature range.
The response may differ outside 1000–1200°C or when processing-induced defects dominate.
Matched thermal histories, inert atmosphere, and matched strain rates provide a controlled HEA-versus-tungsten comparison.
Failure to observe statistically significant improvements in both the mechanical response and the proposed microstructural mediator would falsify the lattice-distortion mechanism.
